summary: The context determines whether continuity means uninterrupted action or an established practice that recurs at appointed times. Psalm 16 describes the speaker’s constant attention to Yahweh.

senses.definition: The speaker keeps Yahweh before him continually. The altar fire must be maintained without going out.
The bread is set before God continually by being renewed each Sabbath. The regular burnt offering consists of a lamb offered each morning and another at twilight.
Daniel describes the taking away of the regular offering. Here the word stands on its own for the established service.

evidence.locator: p. 2695, مَدَّهُ, including prolonging the voice

cognates.note: The Arabic supplies a comparison for extension in time. A historical derivation of the Hebrew noun remains uncertain.

note: The lexicon indexes this noun under מוד. Its historical derivation is uncertain. Habakkuk 3:6 has a disputed verbal form and cannot independently establish the origin of תָּמִיד.
